page.kicker: System · applies without a bot restart
page.infoSub:
All values are stored in the database and apply without a bot restart.
You get IDs in Discord with a right-click → "Copy ID" (developer mode).

permView.areasTip: Who may see or edit which area of the EventHelper
permView.botTip: Who may use which bot command in Discord

page.botCrumb: Access · who may use which bot command in Discord
page.raidChannelSub: The channel a new raid event is created in when none is picked while creating it.
page.raidsheetsSub: Google Sheets by content (tier 4/5 etc.). When filling, the matching sheet is suggested by its keywords. A fixed sheet for a whole raid category is assigned under Categories.
page.topItemsSub: The really big drops — weapons, legendary parts, anything the guild values highly. When a raid awards one of them, the dashboard highlights the award. Which loot addon a category uses is set under Categories.
page.logChannelsSub: Channels where Warcraft Logs are posted automatically. The bot adds the evaluation buttons there.
page.appChannelSub: Channel where new applications are posted as a thread.
page.officerRoleSub: Pinged on new applications. Leave empty for no ping.

overlap.label: {both} of {total}
overlap.tip: {both} of {total} members of the event Discord are on the communication Discord too. Whoever is missing gets pings as a DM later.

drift.noneTip: All synced roles match their source role.
drift.tip: The sync only adds and never removes. Whoever lost the source role keeps the synced one until someone removes it in Discord.

overviewBadge.title: Raid overview
overviewBadge.notSetSub: Pick a communication Discord and a channel for the overview.
overviewBadge.notPostedSub: It is posted on the next run (every 5 minutes) — or now with "Repost".
overviewBadge.currentSub: Updates on signups and sign-offs, new events and every 5 minutes.

dashboard.label: Overview
dashboard.description: Home page with key figures, upcoming and past events.

signup.label: Profile & signup
signup.description: Your own raider profile (characters, specs with gear state, availability, wishes) and your own signup for upcoming raids. Always only your own account.

recruitment.label: Recruitment
recruitment.description: Application templates and posted recruitment messages.

cla.label: CLA / Logcheck
cla.description: Start log evaluations, manage and assign reports.

raids.label: Raid events
raids.description: Create raid events, fill setups, post calls and Softres.

history.label: History & loot
history.description: Loot import, event and character history.

loot.label: Loot views
loot.description: Only the loot tabs of the history: imported loot, latest loot, loot reasons and items — without import, logs and raid lists.

lootcouncil.label: Loot council
lootcouncil.description: Caster overview for the loot council: awarded items per content, BiS gaps and upgrade suggestions.

settings.label: Settings
settings.description: Bot configuration. Admin roles and permissions stay reserved for full admins.

ui.adminOnlySub: Roles with write access to "Settings" do not see this block and cannot save it.

fields.topItemsSub: When one of these items is imported, it shows up on the dashboard under "Latest Loot" — with character, raid and date. Without an entry the card stays empty.

raiderChars.title: Assign characters
raiderChars.noRoles: This category has no raider roles yet — pick roles in its row first and save.
raiderChars.noMembers: No members with the assigned roles found.

raidsheets.name: Name (content)
raidsheets.sheetIdSub: The long part of the sheet URL between /d/ and /edit.
raidsheets.gidSub: The number after #gid= in the tab's URL.
raidsheets.keywordsSub: Comma-separated. When a keyword matches the event title, this sheet is suggested automatically.

reminders.title: Reminders
reminders.tipSub: X hours before signup closes to everyone with a raider role who is still missing; Y hours before the raid starts to everyone signed up. Each reminder goes out exactly once and never after the raid has started. Without a signup deadline the raid start counts.
reminders.empty: No raid categories yet — they are switched on under Settings → Categories.
reminders.unknownCategorySub: Category ID {id} — not found (anymore) on the event Discord.
reminders.whereSub: Event channel, ping channel of the communication Discord or both. With "Talk", anyone not on the communication Discord gets a DM.
reminders.noRoleSub: Without a raider role for the category the bot does not know who is missing — the reminder to missing raiders then does not go out.
reminders.missingSub: Hours before signup closes (without a deadline: before the raid starts) to everyone with a raider role who has not reacted yet. Empty = off.
reminders.signedSub: Hours before the raid starts to everyone signed up (including "comes later"). Empty = off.

roleSync.title: Role sync
roleSync.tipSub: Maps a role of the event Discord to a role of the communication Discord. Runs on every role change and every 10 minutes. It only adds and never removes.
roleSync.dirToTalkTip: Whoever has the role on the event Discord gets it on the communication Discord.
roleSync.dirToEventTip: Whoever has the role on the communication Discord gets it on the event Discord.
roleSync.deleteText: Given roles stay as they are — the sync never removes anything.
roleSync.manageMissing: "Manage Roles" is missing on {servers} — the sync gives nothing there.
roleSync.empty: No mapping yet. Without a mapping no roles are given.
roleSync.notOnSource: No longer on the other server. Remove in Discord.
roleSync.lostSource: No longer has @{role}. Remove in Discord.
roleSync.directionSub: The sync only adds. A lost role stays on the other side and shows up as drift.

discordServers.eventTipSub: The event channels and Raid-Helper live here. The menu's admin role check runs against the first configured event server.
discordServers.talkTipSub: This is where people talk: signup via bot and reminders. Empty = everything runs on the event Discord.
discordServers.noteTipSub: Whoever presses "Tentative" or "Decline" in Discord can leave a short message for the raid lead — the bot posts it here. Whether it is asked (required, optional, none) you set per category under Categories.
discordServers.tipSub: The bot can work with several event servers — each with its own event channels, Raid-Helper and optionally its own raid overview — plus one communication Discord for signup via bot and reminders.
discordServers.talkEmpty: Signup and pings run on the event Discord.
discordServers.label: Label
discordServers.labelSub: A short name of your own, helpful once several event servers run.
discordServers.overviewSub: Where this server's raid overview is posted — the communication Discord, another event server or itself.
discordServers.offlineText: No server list without a connection — the IDs can still be entered.
discordServers.pingSub: Channel for reminders and pings. Whoever is not on the server gets them as a DM.

connections.discordSub: Whether the bot is connected and which Raid-Helper server supplies the events. Which Discord server is the event and which the communication Discord is set under Connections › Discord servers. The Raid-Helper API key itself stays in the .env.
connections.battlenetSub: Optional: with Battle.net API access the character history shows the live gear directly, and the loot council can use the Armory as a gear source.
connections.wclSub:
Draws raid DPS, raid HPS and boss health per boss fight in the fight timeline. Everything else in the log analysis keeps running on the v1 key in the .env.
The curves appear from the next evaluation on.
connections.aiSub: Claude words the recommendations from the log analysis in plain language for the raiders. The rules still decide what stood out; nothing goes out without approval.
connections.lootSyncSub: The WoW addon writes the loot from RCLootcouncil and Gargul into its SavedVariables; the sync tool on the raid leader's computer uploads it with one of these tokens. Uploaded raids land in History & loot → Addon inbox.
connections.discordMissing: The bot is not connected right now — server and role lists are missing until it is back online.
connections.raidhelperIdSub: Used for all Raid-Helper API calls (events, setups, signups). The API key itself stays in the .env.
connections.battlenetMissing: Without client ID and secret the character history shows no live gear.
connections.namespaceSub: Empty = automatic (profile-classicann-<region>). Only set it when Blizzard changes the namespace.
connections.battlenetSecretSub: Never shown again. A new value replaces the stored secret.
connections.wclMissing: Without client ID and secret the fight timeline lacks the DPS, HPS and boss health curves.
connections.wclSecretSub: Create a client without a redirect URL under warcraftlogs.com/api/clients, leave "Public Client" off.
connections.aiMissing: Without an API key the recommendations stay with the rule texts.
connections.modelSub: Empty = claude-opus-5. The wording starts on the report page under "Recommendations".
connections.apiKeySub: Never shown again. A new value replaces the stored key.
connections.secretKeep: •••••••• stored — leave empty to keep it
connections.secretNote: Never shown again, only replaced or deleted.

tokens.revokeText: The sync tool using it can no longer upload anything afterwards.
tokens.title: Loot sync tokens
tokens.created: Token "{name}" created — copy it now, the server only keeps a hash.
tokens.newSub: One name per computer, so a single one can be revoked on its own.
tokens.colTokenSub: The last four characters, so several tokens stay distinguishable.

permissions.rowSub: Click: set the whole row to read, write or off
permissions.additiveSub: Whoever has several roles gets the sum of their permissions; base access and single accounts come on top and never take anything away. Changes apply to signed-in users within about 5 minutes.
permissions.additive: Permissions add up across all roles
permissions.adminsSub: Members with one of these roles have write access to every area and are the only ones with access to permissions and connection secrets. Changes apply within about 5 minutes without signing in again.
permissions.noRolesSub: Server chosen and bot online? The choice is available once the bot is connected.
permissions.emergencySub: The ADMIN_USER_ID from the .env always keeps full access, whatever is set here.
permissions.emergency: Emergency access via ADMIN_USER_ID always remains
permissions.baseSub: Applies to every Discord account that signs in — even without a role and without membership on the server. The menu with logout is always reachable; only what is unlocked here becomes visible.
permissions.rolesSub: Roles without admin rights get targeted access to single areas here. Read = view, write = act there too. Permissions and admin roles stay reserved for full admins — a role with write access to Settings cannot grant itself any rights.
permissions.rolesEmpty: No role with its own permissions yet — add one via "Role or account".
permissions.rolesNotLoaded: No roles loaded (server chosen and bot online?).
permissions.usersSub: Permissions for one specific Discord account — for areas that go to named people instead of a group (such as the loot council). Comes on top like the base access and never takes anything away.
permissions.roleAdminSub: Members with this role get full admin access.
permissions.roleGrantSub: The role starts without permissions; the cells of the new row unlock them.
permissions.discordIdSub: In Discord, right-click the user → "Copy ID" (developer mode must be on).
permissions.invalidId: That does not look like a Discord ID (17–20 digits).

categories.stillRhSub: New events of {names} are still created on Raid-Helper. To switch: open the category › New events. The switch-off checklist is under Connections › Raid-Helper.
categories.empty: No categories loaded (server chosen and bot online?). The list appears once the bot is connected.
categories.switchSub: Channels of this category hold raid events.
categories.unknownSub: This ID is configured but no longer exists in Discord. Deselecting and saving removes it.
categories.charsSub: {assigned} of {members} raiders have a fixed character.
categories.raiderRolesSub: Whoever has one of these roles counts as an expected raider for raids of this category (attendance, missing signups, character assignment). Roles with "Raid" in their name are offered.
categories.noRaidRole: No role found whose name contains "Raid".
categories.charsDetailSub: Which character a raider plays in this category. Overrides the automatic detection from past signups on the event detail page.
categories.newEventsSub: Where new events of this category are created. Raid-Helper events stay in use either way – in lists, attendance, log and loot assignment.
categories.setupDmsSub: After release, every raider of an EventHelper event gets a DM: "You are in group 2 as a healer" or "Bench this time". On a new release only those whose spot changed get another one. The setup in the channel is always posted.
categories.announceSub: A new EventHelper event posts a short line with title, date and signup link and pings the raider roles of this category — exactly once per event, series events included. "Talk"/"both" need a ping channel on the communication Discord.
categories.notesSub: Whoever presses "Tentative" or "Decline" in Discord gets a field for a short message to the raid lead. The bot posts it in the channel you pick under Connections › Discord servers — or below in one of this category's own. "none" does not ask and posts nothing.
categories.noteChannelSub: Where this category's messages go. "Default" is the channel under Connections › Discord servers. A channel the bot can no longer reach falls back to the default.
categories.unreachableSub: The bot does not see this channel (anymore) or may not write there. Messages go to the default channel meanwhile.
categories.discordEventSub: For every EventHelper event of this category the bot creates a Discord event (server sidebar, mobile app). It follows moves, cancellations and deletions. Signup still runs only through the message in the channel — "Interested" does not count. The bot needs the "Manage Events" permission for it.
categories.raidArtSub: Below the signup message there is a picture of the raid (Blizzard's zone picture of the evening's largest instance). An event with its own banner keeps it.
categories.titleSizeSub: How large the letter tiles of the title in the signup message are. "very large" wraps a long title into two lines sooner.
categories.voiceSub: Where the raids of this category meet. Preset when creating an event — still changeable there. Shown in the signup message and the location of the Discord event.
categories.lootAddonSub: Preselects the matching parser on loot import and tells the loot tab of the raid detail page which export to expect.
categories.lootSystemSub: Decides what a raid of this category offers: only with Softres is there the Softres step, "Softres missing" and the Softres list in the menu. "automatic" = {auto}. Single raids can be switched on their page or have Softres added.
categories.templateSub: The raid template a new event of this category starts from. While it is the default it cannot be deleted. You maintain templates under Raid events › Raid templates.
categories.fixedSheetSub: Every raid of this category links this sheet — unless one was created for the raid itself. Templates by keyword: Modules › Raidsheets.
categories.noneShown: No raid category yet — switch on a Discord category below.

folded.one: {count} more Discord category without raid events
folded.other: {count} more Discord categories without raid events

modeTip.everyone: Every member may use the command.
modeTip.roles: Only members with one of the chosen roles (on the event server).
modeTip.admins: Admins only: ADMIN_USER_ID and the admin roles from "Access".

botCommands.unknownRoleSub: Role ID {id} — no longer exists on the event server.
botCommands.title: Bot commands
botCommands.tipSub: Who may use which command in Discord. Buttons and selects of a command inherit its permission. Admins may always do everything.
botCommands.loadError: Could not load the bot commands: {message}
botCommands.noRoles: No roles loaded — is the bot online and the event server chosen?
botCommands.savedGroup: Saved for all commands of the group.
botCommands.rolesSub: Roles of the event server. Whoever has one of them may use the command.
botCommands.wholeGroup: apply to all {count} commands of the group

retirement.title: Switching from Raid-Helper
retirement.optionalTip: Recommendation – switching off does not depend on it.
retirement.switchDisabled: Raid-Helper is no longer queried. The history stays readable; switching back on works any time.
retirement.switchReady: All required items done. Switching off stops all requests to Raid-Helper; past raids stay readable.
retirement.importNothingNew: Nothing new – {count} events are already imported.
retirement.importDry: {events} events · {entries} entries for {users} raiders would be saved.
retirement.whatSub: Only who signed up with which spec – no events, no signups. From that, the one-click signup and the profile suggest the spec played last. An event is never counted twice; a second import only fetches new raids.
retirement.dryFirst: Only the dry run shows what would be saved. Nothing is saved until "Import".
retirement.liveText: Raid-Helper does not answer – only the stored events were read.
retirement.skippedSub: These events were counted in an earlier import and are skipped.
retirement.offText: The EventHelper then no longer queries Raid-Helper: no new Raid-Helper events, no signups, no scan. Past raids stay readable with their stored signups. Switching back on works any time.
retirement.onText: Events, signups and the scan then run through Raid-Helper again.
retirement.infoSub: What should be done before the EventHelper replaces Raid-Helper completely. The two required items unlock the switch below; the rest makes the raiders' everyday life easier. Each item explains itself in the tooltip of its name.
